reviewContext.userProblem: nodetto-cli ddl --page already accepts a page id, short id or exact page name (resolvePageQuery), but --frame only accepts the exact full frame id (apps/cli/src/commands.ts ddlCommand: editor.store.get(frameId)), so scripts that keep human-readable configuration must map frame names to auto-assigned opaque ids themselves.
requiredOutcomes: ddl --page <page> --frame <exact frame name> emits the same DDL as passing that frame's full id.
A unique short-id prefix (at least MIN_PREFIX = 6 characters) of a frame id works for --frame.
Resolution is scoped to the selected --page in the order: exact full id, exact frame name (semantic.name), unique id prefix; frames on other pages never match.

A value that matches no frame, or a name/prefix that matches two or more frames, exits EXIT_ERROR (2) with empty stdout, no --output write, and stderr starting with '--frame must identify a frame on the selected --page.' followed by candidate lines '  <short>\t<name> (full id: <id>)'.

ddl help documents --frame <id|short-id|name>; pages and ddl help state that page and element ids are auto-assigned, opaque and unchanging, rename-page changes only the display name, and names are the human-facing key; the README scoped schema export example uses a frame name.

designDecisionsAndRationale: One private resolveFrameQuery(document, page, query): Resolution placed directly above ddlCommand in apps/cli/src/commands.ts, mirroring resolvePageQuery precedence and selectPage candidate format (design 'ddl --frame resolution').
Short ids are shortIds over all document element ids so candidate listings match inspect output; MIN_PREFIX is reused from apps/cli/src/ids.ts.
Name matching is exact and case-sensitive like page names; an ambiguous name fails and does not fall through to prefix matching, so the CLI never silently picks a frame.
The first failure line keeps the current wording, which the existing 'DDL frame scopes ...' test asserts.
Help/docs text and its test are a separate plan with disjoint files so both plans run in one parallel wave.
intentionalTradeoffs: Name-before-prefix precedence: a frame named like another frame's id prefix resolves by name; the full id always resolves (covered by a separate fixture).
Prefixes shorter than 6 characters never match, even if unique on the page.
supportedEdgeCases: Two frames sharing a name on the page (ambiguous, lists only matching frames).
Same-name frame on another page is never matched; a full id from another page fails.
Non-frame element ids (for example t-users) are never candidates.
Page with no frames reports 'Page "<name>" has no frames.'.
Missing or empty frame names display as (unnamed); non-string names are guarded.
--output is not written on resolution failure.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Frame name resolution for commands other than ddl.
